description: Renders a registered Open Design artifact in a headless browser (an installed Chrome, Edge, or Chromium) and returns what it looks like: screenshots attached as images, plus preflight findings (overflow and clipped text, contrast, text overlap, safe area, broken images/fonts, emoji, QR codes, and horizontal-scroll for pages that scroll sideways). Leaves the artifact and its manifest alone; saves the run's screenshots under .open-design/.checks/ so the user can see them, before and after, in the browser preview's Checks panel or at the listed paths. Call it after creating or substantially editing an artifact and registering it, before telling the user it's done: fix every ERROR, look at the screenshots for what the checks can't measure (balance, hierarchy, crowded or empty areas, text over busy imagery), then re-check — at most two fix rounds; tell the user about anything left. For a 3D design with a review sheet, a clean check isn't the end: get the critique the result asks for, for up to three critique rounds. What it renders: a page without a [data-od-card] at each viewport (default desktop 1440×900 and mobile 390×844, findings tagged by viewport); a card design (poster, social post) at its registered format size; a deck slide by slide (findings tagged by slide, one contact sheet of up to 12 slides — pass slides to see others). Screenshots are JPEG with a long edge of at most 1568 px; maxImages (default 3, max 6) bounds how many are attached, and 0 returns findings only. Returns a 'no-browser' error when no browser is installed: then skip the check and tell the user once that visual checking needs Chrome, Edge or Chromium. For bulk data rows or shape sheets, use export_open_design_artifact with checkOnly instead. A 3D scene that exposes window.odScene.scene, camera and renderer (the 3d-object ready contract) also gets a review sheet, one image showing the overview, close-up, low-angle and wireframe views (placed second), plus 3D evidence (pixel metrics, renderer statistics) and a webgl-budget warning for scenes too heavy for software rendering; views picks which views go on the sheet, or false for none.

at.description: Animations: up to 6 times in seconds. Also captures the artifact at those moments on a virtual clock (labelled t=<seconds>s), so you can see the start, middle and end of an animation. They share maxImages with the regular screenshots.

entryPath.description: Workspace-relative path to the registered artifact's entry file.

maxImages.description: How many screenshots to attach (default 3). 0 returns findings only.

slides.description: Decks only: 1-based slide numbers to check (default every slide; the contact sheet shows the first 12 of them).

viewports.description: Pages without a card only: 1–4 viewports to check instead of the default desktop 1440×900 and mobile 390×844.

name.description: Label used in findings and screenshots, e.g. "tablet".

views.description: 3D scenes exposing window.odScene.scene/camera/renderer: which review views to put on the sheet (default all four: overview, closeup, low, wireframe), or false for no sheet.

name: check_open_design_artifact
